liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (2 reviews): The Greatest Story into West L.A. Fadeaway pairing is very good, according to the reviewer; Greatest Story is possibly the best of 1994, with Jerry stepping up on wah wah [8][9]
- **Victim or the Crime** (2 reviews): Victim or the Crime is solid but not fully explored, in the reviewer's view; Victim or the Crime has a notably spacey opening [6][16]
- **Foolish Heart** (2 reviews): Jerry's Foolish Heart solo builds slowly and improvisationally, with many teases, while the whole band stays together; The Foolish Heart solo is sweet; Jerry mumbles lyrics around it, but the instrumental break sounds great [8][15]
- **Let the Good Times Roll** (1 review): Jerry sounds good right from the opening Let the Good Times Roll [7]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Bertha has extended Jerry solos and a faster tempo than usual, as he also played at Landover and NYC [9]
- **El Paso** (1 review): Bobby plays acoustic guitar on El Paso [16]
- **Eternity** (1 review): The reviewer calls Eternity a keeper, one of the points where the show finally picks up [6]
- **Jam** (1 review): The short jam after Samba in the Rain, before Drums, is singled out as great [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **Looks Like Rani**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]

## The recordings

- **gd94-09-28.pmb.pujol.14945.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 160 min; rated 3/5 by 8 [1]. Said about its sound: The audience recording sounds good for the Garden [7]
- **gd1994-09-28.akg460.flaschner.sobel.83238.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 163 min [2]
- **gd1994-09-28.152489.senn-me88.rogosa.miller.sirmick.flac1648**: source not stated; 20 songs; 160 min [3]
- **gd1994-09-28.136872.sbd.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 154 min; rated 1.8/5 by 5 [4]

## Around the show

- The drummers tried to come out on stage, with Jerry and Vince protesting, leading into a juicy jam [6]
- The reviewer ranks this Foolish Heart as their favorite version ever [8]
- The reviewer says this was the night the Boston run took off, with the band playing strongly from the start [9]
- The reviewer finds this show better than the previous night's [14]
- The reviewer ranks this Foolish Heart among the top five so far [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd94-09-28.pmb.pujol.14945.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Dave Minor; transferred by Marc Pujol; source: Audience: PMB Microphones [1]. Also: Recorded with PMB shotgun capsules into an Advent preamp, then an attenuator, then a Kenwood DAT; Scott is credited; PMB mics were made by a defunct German company; they are self-powered, with shotgun capsules and small figure-8 capsules [1][10]
- **gd1994-09-28.akg460.flaschner.sobel.83238.flac16**: taped by Dave Flaschner; transferred by Jason Sobel; source: AKG 460B/ck61 > custom pre-amp > Sony D7 (@ 48kHz) [2]. Also: Transferred from a master DAT tape borrowed from Dave; the original 48 kHz wav files are archived [2]
- **gd1994-09-28.152489.senn-me88.rogosa.miller.sirmick.flac1648**: taped by Dan Rogosa; transferred by Sirmick and Charlie Miller; source: Sennheiser ME88's > Sony TCD-D7 > DAT Master (48k) [3]
- **gd1994-09-28.136872.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Dat -> Cassette Master -> Dat (44.1k) [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1994-09-28 Wed Boston Garden, Boston, MA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1307195043803/grateful-dead-1994-09-28-wed-boston) [19]
